mechanism: Senicapoc is an oral selective blocker of the intermediate-conductance calcium-activated potassium channel KCa3.1, also called the Gardos channel. In sickle cell disease, Gardos-channel blockade is intended to reduce red blood cell potassium and water loss, limit red cell dehydration and hemolysis, and increase hemoglobin by improving sickle red blood cell survival.
development_status: ClinicalTrials.gov lists RESCUE (NCT07282210; SIL-8301-001) as a not yet recruiting Phase 2 randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled study sponsored by Biossil Inc. Estimated enrollment is 105 patients aged 16 to 35 years with sickle cell disease, Hb <= 9.0 g/dL, no more than one acute SCD-related painful crisis per year over the preceding 2 years, at least one hemolytic complication, and current hydroxyurea use. The trial evaluates senicapoc 20 mg twice daily for 4 days followed by 10 mg once daily for up to 24 weeks versus placebo, with primary completion estimated in November 2028 and study completion in January 2029. No ClinicalTrials.gov results are posted.
expected_launch_window: 2031-2033 if Phase 2 confirms hemoglobin/hemolysis benefit and a registrational strategy is accepted
clinical_summary: RESCUE is focused on a hemolytic SCD endotype rather than a high-VOC population, with primary efficacy based on the proportion of patients achieving >1 g/dL Hb increase at 24 weeks. This directly addresses the historical senicapoc signal: prior Phase 2 data showed high-dose senicapoc improved Hb by 0.68 g/dL versus 0.01 g/dL for placebo and improved dense RBCs, reticulocytes, LDH, and indirect bilirubin; a later Phase 3 crisis-rate trial improved anemia/hemolysis markers but was stopped for low probability of reducing acute pain crises. Reanalysis/contextual literature suggests a >1 g/dL Hb response in 34% of senicapoc-treated Phase 3 patients treated at least 24 weeks versus 6% on placebo. Differentiation would be meaningful if replicated in the selected hemolytic phenotype, especially after voxelotor withdrawal, but current evidence remains biomarker-led and the new Biossil trial has not begun reporting results.
safety_summary: Prior Phase 2 publication described senicapoc as safe and well tolerated over 12 weeks. The prior Phase 3 program was terminated for low probability of achieving the pain-crisis endpoint rather than a clearly reported senicapoc safety failure. Current RESCUE safety outcomes include incidence of adverse events, serious adverse events, and SCD-related adverse events through 28 weeks, but no results are posted. Regulatory scrutiny of hemoglobin-surrogate SCD drugs is higher after Oxbryta's 2024 voluntary market withdrawal for safety concerns, so hemolysis and vaso-occlusive outcomes will need close review.
management_tools: Pharmacy-benefit prior authorization for FDA-approved SCD indication and final labeled endotype
Require diagnosis of sickle cell disease and baseline hemolytic phenotype documentation such as Hb <= 9 g/dL and qualifying hemolytic complication if label follows RESCUE design
Require concomitant or prior hydroxyurea criteria aligned to final label and plan design
Hematologist or sickle-cell specialist prescribing or consultation
Baseline and follow-up hemoglobin, reticulocyte count, bilirubin, LDH, renal/albuminuria markers, and transfusion history documentation
Continuation criteria requiring documented Hb response, hemolysis-marker improvement, absence of excess SCD complications, and acceptable tolerability
Quantity limit aligned to labeled tablet strength, loading dose, and maintenance dose
Concurrent therapy review for overlapping SCD disease-modifying agents and transfusion programs
evidence_gaps: NCT07282210 is not yet recruiting and has no posted efficacy or safety results.
No public Biossil price, launch timing, pivotal-trial plan, or regulatory-pathway statement for SIL-8301 in SCD was found.

The current Phase 2 trial uses a selected hemolytic phenotype and Hb-response primary endpoint, so generalizability to broader SCD and effects on VOCs, acute chest syndrome, kidney outcomes, pulmonary hypertension, and survival remain unknown.
Prior senicapoc Phase 3 testing failed to reduce acute painful crises despite Hb and hemolysis improvements.
Annual cost is analog-derived from current oral SCD therapy pricing and withdrawn voxelotor WAC; actual senicapoc net cost, gross price, rebates, and duration are unknown.
ClinicalTrials.gov marks the RESCUE study as not FDA-regulated drug, which should be rechecked if U.S. sites or an IND-regulated pathway are later disclosed.

sources.title: Efficacy and Safety of SIL-8301 for Control of Hemolysis in a Uniform Sickle Cell Disease Endotype
supports: ClinicalTrials.gov ID NCT07282210, study ID SIL-8301-001, acronym RESCUE, sponsor Biossil Inc.
Official title is a multicenter randomized double-blind placebo-controlled study of SIL-8301 in SCD patients with a predominantly hemolytic phenotype.
Overall status is not yet recruiting; Phase 2; estimated enrollment is 105; estimated start is January 2026; estimated primary completion is November 2028; estimated completion is January 2029.
Intervention is senicapoc 10 mg tablets, administered as 20 mg twice daily for 4 days followed by 10 mg once daily for up to 24 weeks; comparator is matching placebo.
Primary outcome is Hb response rate, defined as the proportion of participants achieving an increase in Hb of >1 g/dL from baseline at 24 weeks.

Secondary outcomes include hemolytic markers, Hb increase >2 g/dL, uACR, 6-minute walk test, ASCQ-ME, PROMIS, SCD complication rate, global impression of change, acute SCD-related painful crisis frequency, and AEs/SAEs/SCD-related AEs.

Eligibility includes age 16 to 35 years, documented SCD, Hb <= 9.0 g/dL, no more than one acute SCD-related painful crisis requiring a medical-facility visit per year in the prior 2 years, history of at least one hemolytic complication, and current hydroxyurea treatment.
ClinicalTrials.gov hasResults is false; the registry marks the study as not FDA-regulated drug and not FDA-regulated device.

sources.title: Biossil Home Page
supports: Biossil describes itself as an AI-native biopharma company based in Toronto.
The company states it is advancing late-stage programs in life-threatening indications with urgent unmet needs.
Biossil lists active trials as ongoing in sickle cell disease, idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis, glioblastoma, breast cancer, and Alzheimer's disease.
The site lists Ataga 2021 among peer-reviewed links relevant to its pipeline.

sources.title: A Study of the Efficacy and Safety of ICA-17043 (With or Without Hydroxyurea) in Patients With Sickle Cell Anemia
supports: Completed Phase 2 study sponsored by Icagen with actual enrollment of 90 patients.
ICA-17043 was described as a potent and specific inhibitor of a channel in human RBCs that blocks RBC dehydration.
Primary efficacy endpoint was change from baseline in hemoglobin over 12 weeks.
Arms included 6 mg/day senicapoc, 10 mg/day senicapoc, and placebo, with loading doses before maintenance treatment.
Secondary outcomes included other hematologic measures, RBC indices, bilirubin, LDH, painful-crisis rate and timing, pain intensity, quality of life, health economic data, and plasma concentration.

sources.title: Efficacy and safety of the Gardos channel blocker, senicapoc (ICA-17043), in patients with sickle cell anemia
supports: Twelve-week multicenter Phase 2 randomized, double-blind, dose-finding study evaluated senicapoc safety and effect on hemoglobin and hemolysis markers in sickle cell anemia.
Patients were randomized to placebo, 6 mg/day senicapoc, or 10 mg/day senicapoc.
High-dose senicapoc improved mean hemoglobin by 0.68 g/dL versus 0.01 g/dL for placebo, P < .001.
High-dose senicapoc significantly decreased dense RBC percentage, reticulocytes, LDH, and indirect bilirubin compared with placebo.
The publication concluded senicapoc was safe and well tolerated and suggested increased sickle RBC survival.

sources.title: A Stratified Sickle Event Randomized Trial (ASSERT)
supports: Phase 3 ASSERT trial of ICA-17043 in SCD was sponsored by Icagen.
Overall status is terminated with actual enrollment of 297 and actual completion in June 2007.
The trial was stopped because of low probability of achieving the primary endpoint.
Primary outcome was sickle cell crisis rate over 52 weeks.

The brief summary states the trial compared ICA-17043 to placebo with or without hydroxyurea in patients with SCD who had two or more acute sickle-related painful crises requiring a medical-facility visit within the prior 12 months.

sources.title: Improvements in haemolysis and indicators of erythrocyte survival do not correlate with acute vaso-occlusive crises in patients with sickle cell disease
supports: Phase 3 randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind trial evaluated the Gardos channel blocker senicapoc in SCD.
Senicapoc selectively blocks potassium efflux through the Gardos channel, reducing RBC dehydration and hemolysis and increasing hemoglobin levels in SCD.
A total of 145 patients were randomized to senicapoc and 144 to placebo for 52 weeks.
Patients receiving senicapoc had significant increases in hematocrit and hemoglobin and decreases in dense erythrocytes and reticulocytes compared with placebo.

The unblinded Data Monitoring Committee terminated the study early for lack of efficacy because no significant improvement in sickle cell painful-crisis rate was observed despite improvements in anemia and hemolysis.

sources.title: The challenge of clinical end points in sickle cell disease
supports: The review states senicapoc improved anemia and hemolysis in SCD, but the Phase 3 trial did not significantly reduce acute pain episodes versus placebo.
It identifies hemoglobin and complications related to hemolysis, such as stroke risk and chronic kidney disease, as alternative endpoints relevant to senicapoc.

It reports that reanalysis of Phase 3 senicapoc data found >1 g/dL hemoglobin response from baseline in 29 of 85 patients (34%) in the senicapoc arm versus 6% in the placebo group among patients treated at least 24 weeks.
It notes that the reanalysis showed more pronounced improvement in hemolysis markers than voxelotor, while acknowledging the absence of acute pain episode reduction.

sources.title: Endari: Package Insert / Prescribing Information
supports: Endari is indicated to reduce acute complications of sickle cell disease in adults and pediatric patients 5 years and older.
Recommended dosing is 5 g to 15 g orally twice daily by body weight.
The label describes 5 g packets and 2 to 6 packets per day depending on body weight.
Common adverse reactions include constipation, nausea, headache, abdominal pain, cough, pain in extremity, back pain, and chest pain.
Clinical studies included Phase 3 and Phase 2 placebo-controlled trials, with most patients receiving hydroxyurea at baseline.

sources.title: L-glutamine (Endari): Uses, Side Effects, Dosage and More
supports: GoodRx lists l-glutamine (Endari) as used for sickle cell disease.
GoodRx states typical dosage for people over 143 lb is 15 g, or 3 packets, twice daily.
GoodRx lists average retail price of $3,676.66 for 180 packets of 5 g l-glutamine (Endari), with a lower coupon price also shown.
The 180-packet quantity corresponds to a 30-day supply for the highest labeled Endari body-weight band.

sources.title: Information for Colorado Prescribers of Prescription Drugs: OXBRYTA
supports: Pfizer Colorado price disclosure listed Oxbryta 500 mg tablet WAC at $12,114.20 per 90-tablet package.
The disclosure states WAC is the published list price to wholesalers before discounts, rebates, or other price reductions.
The disclosure states WAC may differ significantly from actual prices paid by customers and consumers.

sources.title: FDA is alerting patients and health care professionals about the voluntary withdrawal of Oxbryta from the market due to safety concerns
supports: FDA alerted patients and health care professionals that Oxbryta was being voluntarily withdrawn from the market by the manufacturer due to safety concerns.
FDA stated recent data indicated the benefit of Oxbryta did not outweigh risks for the sickle cell patient population.
FDA stated postmarketing clinical trials reported higher vaso-occlusive crisis rates and more deaths in Oxbryta-treated patients compared with placebo.
FDA noted Oxbryta had accelerated approval based on a surrogate or intermediate clinical endpoint reasonably likely to predict clinical benefit.

sources.title: Sickle Cell Disease - L-glutamine Prior Authorization Policy
supports: Cigna recommends prior authorization for prescription benefit coverage of l-glutamine oral powder.
Coverage for sickle cell disease requires documentation, age at least 5 years, and prescribing by or in consultation with a physician who specializes in sickle cell disease such as a hematologist.
L-glutamine is considered not medically necessary for uses other than covered FDA-approved or supported uses.
Cigna notes approval duration of 1 year.

sources.title: CVS Caremark Specialty Guideline Management: L-glutamine powder-Endari
supports: CVS Caremark states Endari is indicated to reduce acute complications of SCD in adults and pediatric patients 5 years and older.
The medication must be prescribed by or in consultation with a hematologist or specialist in sickle cell disease.
Initial authorization for HbSS or sickle beta-0 thalassemia can require inadequate response/intolerance to hydroxyurea, hydroxyurea contraindication, or use with concurrent hydroxyurea.

Continuation authorization may be granted when the member has experienced reduced acute complications such as painful vaso-occlusive episodes, acute chest syndrome, fever, priapism, or splenic sequestration.

expected_launch_window.value: 2031-2033 if Phase 2 confirms hemoglobin/hemolysis benefit and a registrational strategy is accepted
expected_launch_window.method: Derived from not-yet-recruiting Phase 2 status, estimated November 2028 primary completion, need for data readout and likely registrational confirmation, and heightened regulatory scrutiny after Oxbryta's surrogate-endpoint withdrawal.
expected_launch_window.explanation: A launch before 2031 is unlikely because RESCUE has not begun recruiting and is not a registrational Phase 3 trial. Prior senicapoc Phase 3 data may support the rationale, but the prior study failed on pain-crisis reduction and the current endpoint strategy still requires validation.

annual_cost_range.method: Used oral SCD therapy analogs because senicapoc has no disclosed price: low estimate equals Endari average retail $3,676.66 per 180 packets x 12 months = $44,119.92; high estimate equals Oxbryta 500 mg WAC $12,114.20 per 90-tablet monthly package x 12 months = $145,370.40.
annual_cost_range.explanation: The range reflects plausible gross annual oral SCD specialty-drug pricing and excludes rebates, discounts, dispensing fees, monitoring, acute-care costs, transfusions, and patient assistance. Oxbryta is withdrawn and used only as a historical oral hemoglobin-focused SCD cost analog.

clinical_differentiation.method: Weighted oral Gardos-channel mechanism, prior Hb and hemolysis-marker effects, new enrichment for a hemolytic phenotype, and post-Oxbryta unmet need against absence of new Phase 2 results and prior failure on pain-crisis reduction.
clinical_differentiation.explanation: Senicapoc could be meaningfully differentiated for a hemolytic SCD subset if RESCUE reproduces Hb and hemolysis responses without excess VOC or mortality risk, but it is not yet proven to improve hard clinical outcomes.

budget_impact.method: Assessed chronic oral specialty-drug use, analog gross annual cost of about $44k to $145k, small selected SCD hemolytic population, likely pharmacy-benefit routing, and availability of standard PA/specialist controls.
budget_impact.explanation: Per-patient spend could be material, but the trial targets a narrowed phenotype and payer tools for SCD oral disease-modifying therapies already exist.

disruption_risk.method: Balanced early not-yet-recruiting Phase 2 timing against a plausible post-Oxbryta gap for oral hemoglobin/hemolysis-directed SCD therapy and the need to monitor surrogate-endpoint safety.
disruption_risk.explanation: Near-term disruption is limited, but positive RESCUE results could require payer policy work around endotype documentation, response monitoring, hydroxyurea positioning, and safety surveillance.

recommended_action.method: Recommended action reflects not-yet-recruiting Phase 2 status, no posted results, estimated 2028 primary completion, unresolved regulatory path, and known historical efficacy/safety context.
recommended_action.explanation: Track recruitment, protocol updates, Phase 2 Hb and hemolysis results, VOC and mortality imbalance checks, and any Biossil regulatory announcements before drafting active launch policies.

quality_flags: Current evidence gap: NCT07282210 is not yet recruiting and has no posted results.
Endpoint risk: the current trial uses Hb response and hemolysis-focused enrichment, while prior Phase 3 senicapoc testing failed to reduce acute sickle painful crises.

Regulatory context risk: Oxbryta, another oral SCD drug approved using a hemoglobin surrogate endpoint, was voluntarily withdrawn in 2024 after postmarketing data showed higher vaso-occlusive crisis rates and more deaths versus placebo.
ClinicalTrials.gov marks NCT07282210 as not FDA-regulated drug; recheck if U.S. sites, IND status, or regulatory submissions become public.
Annual cost estimate is analog-derived and uses Endari current retail pricing plus withdrawn Oxbryta historical WAC; actual senicapoc price and net payer cost are unknown.
Biossil's public website provides broad pipeline positioning but does not disclose detailed SIL-8301 SCD launch timing, pricing, or registrational strategy.
